title: Ecuador's Banana Export Boom Begins
note: Boom onset confirmed late 1940s/early 1950s under Galo Plaza. Ecuador became world's largest exporter by 1952.

title: Ecuador Declares 200-Mile Maritime Zone (Declaration of Santiago)
note: Santiago Declaration signed August 18, 1952 by Ecuador, Chile, and Peru. First 200-mile limit in international law.

title: Velasco Ibarra Wins Third Presidential Term
note: Third term began September 1, 1952. Confirmed as his only completed term (1952–1956).

title: Military Coup Ousts Velasco Ibarra
note: No coup in 1953. Velasco Ibarra's third term (1952–1956) was his only completed term. He was not ousted until November 1961. Year is wrong by 8+ years.

title: Ecuador Solidifies Position as World's Largest Banana Exporter
note: Ecuador's ~25% share of global banana trade in mid-1950s confirmed.

title: Galapagos Islands Declared National Park
note: National park established June 15, 1959, protecting 97% of land area.

title: Velasco Ibarra Wins Fourth Term; Ecuador Breaks with Cuba
note: Fourth term and Cuba break confirmed.

title: Military Junta Overthrows President Arosemena
note: Coup occurred July 11, 1963, not 1962. Year is off by 1. A related military rebellion occurred in March 1962 but Arosemena was not overthrown then.

title: Military Junta Abolishes Huasipungo and Enacts Agrarian Reform
note: Junta's agrarian reform abolishing huasipungo confirmed.

title: Amazon Territory Opened for Oil Exploration
note: 1964 Napo Concession granted to Texaco-Gulf consortium confirmed.

title: Military Junta Collapses; Return to Civilian Rule
note: Junta ended 1966 under popular pressure; civilian transition confirmed.

title: Texaco-Gulf Confirms Major Amazon Oil Discovery
note: Major commercial discovery in Lago Agrio area confirmed 1967; new constitution also adopted.

title: Velasco Ibarra Wins Fifth and Final Presidential Term
note: Fifth term 1968 confirmed; dissolved legislature 1970, ousted by coup 1972.

title: Ecuador Joins the Andean Pact (Cartagena Agreement)
note: Andean Pact signed 1969; Ecuador founding member.

title: Military Coup Brings Rodríguez Lara to Power; Oil Exports Begin
note: Coup and SOTE pipeline opening confirmed 1972.

title: CEPE State Oil Company Created
note: CEPE founding 1972 confirmed.

title: Oil Price Shock Fuels State Expansion and Debt Accumulation
note: 1973 Arab oil embargo and Ecuador windfall revenue confirmed.

title: Ecuador Withdraws from OPEC; Failed Counter-Coup Against Rodríguez Lara
note: OPEC withdrawal and failed coup attempt confirmed 1975.

title: Military Triumvirate Pledges Democratic Transition
note: Supreme Council of Government and transition calendar confirmed.

title: Aztra Sugar Mill Massacre
note: October 18, 1977 massacre confirmed; 100+ workers killed in Cañar province.

title: 1978 Constitution Grants Illiterates Right to Vote
note: 1978 constitutional referendum granting illiterate voting rights confirmed.

title: Jaime Roldós Elected; Return to Constitutional Democracy
note: Roldós victory and democratic transition confirmed.

title: President Roldós Dies in Plane Crash; Paquisha Conflict with Peru
note: Roldós plane crash May 24, 1981 and Paquisha border clash confirmed.

title: Latin American Debt Crisis and IMF Structural Adjustment
note: 1982 debt crisis impact on Ecuador and IMF adjustment confirmed.

title: Texaco Amazon Contamination Draws Domestic and International Attention
note: Contamination in Lago Agrio region well documented; scrutiny grew through the 1980s.

title: Febres-Cordero Wins Presidency; Neoliberal Reforms Launched
note: Febres-Cordero election and AVC guerrilla activity confirmed.

title: Oil Price Collapse Devastates Ecuador's Economy; President Briefly Kidnapped
note: 1986 oil price crash and Febres-Cordero hostage incident confirmed.

title: Major Earthquake Destroys SOTE Pipeline; Ecuador Suspends Debt Payments
note: March 5, 1987 earthquakes (6.1 and 6.9 magnitude), ~1,000 deaths, SOTE pipeline destroyed, debt suspension confirmed.

title: Rodrigo Borja Wins Presidency; AVC Guerrilla Demobilized
note: Borja election and AVC demobilization confirmed.

title: CONAIE Founded as National Indigenous Organization
note: CONAIE formally constituted 1986–1989; Wikipedia gives 1986 as founding year but formal consolidation as national umbrella body confirmed late 1980s.

title: First National Indigenous Uprising (Levantamiento Indígena)
note: June 1990 CONAIE uprising confirmed.

title: Texaco Lawsuit Filed in New York Courts
note: Lawsuit filed in New York 1993 per Wikipedia; some sources cite 1991–1993 filing period. Minor uncertainty on exact year but substantively correct.

title: Amazon Indigenous Land Titling March; Ecuador Exits OPEC
note: 1992 march to Quito and OPEC withdrawal confirmed.

title: Durán Ballén Privatization Program and Financial Liberalization
note: Durán Ballén privatization and financial deregulation confirmed.

title: Second Indigenous Uprising Over Land Law; Vice President Dahik Corruption Scandal
note: 1994 indigenous uprising and Dahik flight to Costa Rica confirmed.

title: Cenepa War with Peru
note: January–March 1995 war confirmed. Death toll estimates vary widely (official claims ~80–110, independent estimates up to 500+); '400+ troops' figure is within range.

title: Abdalá Bucaram Elected President; Implements Austerity Despite Populism
note: Bucaram election and austerity U-turn confirmed.

title: Bucaram Removed; Mass Protests and First Female President
note: February 1997 removal, Arteaga presidency (2 days), Alarcón interim all confirmed.

title: Brasília Peace Agreement Permanently Resolves Ecuador-Peru Border Dispute
note: October 26, 1998 Brasília agreement confirmed.

title: Banking Crisis Erupts; 1998 Constitution Adopted
note: Banking crisis onset and 1998 constitution confirmed.

title: Total Economic and Financial Collapse; Mass Emigration Wave
note: GDP contraction, sucre collapse, bank holiday, and emigration wave confirmed.

title: Military-Indigenous Coup Ousts Mahuad; Ecuador Adopts the US Dollar
note: January 2000 coup and dollarization at 25,000 sucres per dollar confirmed.

title: OCP Heavy Crude Pipeline Construction Begins
note: OCP construction start 2001, completed 2003, confirmed.

title: Lucio Gutiérrez Elected President with Indigenous Support
note: Gutiérrez election with CONAIE/Pachakutik support confirmed.

title: Gutiérrez Ousted by 'Forajidos' Uprising; Occidental Petroleum Expelled
note: April 2005 forajidos uprising, Palacio succession, and Occidental contract cancellation confirmed.

title: Rafael Correa Wins Presidential Election; Ecuador Exits US FTA Talks
note: November 2006 Correa election and FTA exit confirmed.

title: Yasuni-ITT Initiative Proposed; Ecuador Joins ALBA
note: Yasuni-ITT proposal and ALBA joining confirmed.

title: 2008 Constitution Enshrines Rights of Nature; Ecuador Defaults on External Debt
note: Montecristi constitution (64% approval), rights of nature, Colombia bombing of FARC on Ecuadorian soil, and $3.2B debt default all confirmed.

title: Correa Closes US Manta Air Base; Ecuador Rejoins OPEC
note: Manta base closure and OPEC rejoining confirmed.

title: Police Uprising (30-S) Briefly Traps Correa; Social Spending Surge
note: September 30, 2010 police strike and hospital siege confirmed.

title: Lago Agrio Court Issues $9.5 Billion Judgment Against Chevron
note: February 2011 judgment ($18B initial, reduced to $9.5B) confirmed. US courts ruled unenforceable due to fraud.

title: Julian Assange Granted Asylum in Ecuador's London Embassy
note: Asylum granted 2012; Assange remained until 2019.

title: Correa Wins Third Term; Yasuni-ITT Abandoned and Amazon Drilling Authorized
note: 57% first-round victory and Yasuni ITT abandonment confirmed.

title: Oil Price Decline Begins; China Financing Expands; Indigenous Mining Protests
note: Oil price decline from mid-2014 and Chinese oil-backed financing confirmed.

title: Massive Anti-Correa Protests; Cotopaxi Volcano Reactivates
note: June 2015 protests over inheritance/capital gains taxes and Cotopaxi reactivation confirmed.

title: 7.8 Magnitude Earthquake Kills 650 in Manabí Province
note: April 16, 2016, 7.8 Mw earthquake confirmed; 676 killed (event says 650+, consistent).

title: Lenin Moreno Wins Presidency; Breaks with Correa
note: Moreno election and rupture with Correa confirmed.

title: Three Journalists Kidnapped and Killed Near Colombian Border
note: Three El Comercio journalists kidnapped and killed by dissident FARC confirmed.

title: October Uprising Against Fuel Subsidy Cuts Forces Government Reversal
note: 11-day uprising, 8 killed, 1,340 injured, 1,192 detained, Moreno reversal confirmed.

title: COVID-19 Overwhelms Guayaquil; Economy Contracts 7.8%
note: Guayaquil collapse and GDP contraction ~7.8% confirmed.

title: Guillermo Lasso Wins Presidency; Prison Massacres Expose Gang Penetration
note: Lasso election and February 2021 prison massacre (80+ killed in one day) confirmed.

title: 18-Day Indigenous Uprising Forces 218-Point Agreement; Organized Crime Escalates
note: June 2022 uprising, 218-point agreement, and homicide rate surge confirmed.

title: Lasso Invokes 'Muerte Cruzada'; Villavicencio Assassinated; Noboa Elected
note: Muerte cruzada, Villavicencio assassination (August 9), and Noboa election all confirmed.

title: Historic Referendum Votes to Halt Yasuni Amazon Oil Drilling
note: August 2023 referendum (~59% yes) to halt ITT block drilling confirmed.

title: TC Televisión Siege; Noboa Declares Internal Armed Conflict
note: January 9, 2024 TC Televisión seizure and internal armed conflict declaration confirmed.

title: Ecuador Invades Mexican Embassy to Arrest Former Vice President Glas
note: April 5, 2024 embassy raid and Mexico breaking diplomatic relations confirmed.

title: Noboa Re-elected in Landslide; Energy Crisis Hits Nationwide
note: Noboa's re-election occurred in 2025 (first round February 9, 2025; runoff April 13, 2025), not 2024. He won ~55.7% in a runoff, not 84% in a first round. The energy crisis details (up to 14-hour blackouts in Oct 2024) are accurate but the election year is wrong by 1 year.
